The record describes an online platform or service that children under 18 can access. In its decision on MediaLab.AI (operator of Imgur), the UK Information Commissioner's Office found that offering an online service to children without a DPIA for that high-risk processing breaches Article 35(1) UK GDPR. It also found that consent does not work as the lawful basis when the platform has no way of verifying a user's age or obtaining parental consent for younger users. That finding cuts against the company's position here. But the outcome depends on this company's own facts: whether age verification and parental-consent mechanisms actually exist and function, and whether a DPIA specifically addressed processing children's data before the service was offered to them. Section 1 records whether that trigger is satisfied. (ICO, MediaLab.AI, Inc., decision of 4 February 2026; supervisory-authority decision — persuasive, non-binding outside its jurisdiction.)
